standards.title: DNA structure
standards.description: Students describe the structure of DNA and how it stores information.
iCan: I can describe a nucleotide (phosphate, deoxyribose sugar, nitrogenous base) and that DNA is a polymer of nucleotides
I can describe the double helix: two antiparallel strands with a sugar-phosphate backbone outside and the paired bases inside
I can state the base-pairing rules (A with T, C with G), held by hydrogen bonds, so the two strands are complementary
I can explain that the base sequence is the stored information, and credit the Watson, Crick, and Franklin model (Franklin's X-ray data)

exam.examItems: MC Q1, Q2, Q3; SA 11, 12; Part 4 Diagram

standards.title: DNA replication
standards.description: Students explain how DNA is copied accurately.
iCan: I can explain that replication is semiconservative: each new molecule keeps one old strand and one new strand
I can name the key players: helicase unwinds, primase lays a primer, DNA polymerase adds nucleotides 5' to 3', ligase seals
I can explain that the leading strand is made continuously and the lagging strand in pieces (Okazaki fragments), because the strands are antiparallel
I can explain that proofreading and repair keep replication accurate, and each base pairs with its complement so the sequence is preserved

standards.title: Transcription
standards.description: Students explain how a gene is transcribed into RNA.
iCan: I can explain that transcription copies a gene's DNA into mRNA using RNA polymerase, with uracil in place of thymine
I can identify the promoter as where RNA polymerase binds and the template strand as the one that is read
I can explain eukaryotic RNA processing: a cap and tail are added, and introns are removed while exons are joined (splicing)
I can state that transcription happens in the nucleus and the finished mRNA leaves for the ribosomes

standards.title: Translation
standards.description: Students explain how mRNA is translated into a protein.
iCan: I can explain that the ribosome reads mRNA in three-base codons, and the genetic code maps each codon to an amino acid (with start and stop codons)
I can explain that a tRNA carries a specific amino acid and has an anticodon that pairs with the codon
I can describe the steps: initiation, elongation (codon by codon, peptide bonds form), and termination at a stop codon
I can connect sequence to function: the codon sequence sets the amino acid sequence, which sets the protein's shape and job (back to Unit 2)

standards.title: Mutations
standards.description: Students explain how changes in DNA affect proteins.
iCan: I can define a mutation as a change in the DNA base sequence
I can distinguish substitutions (silent, missense, nonsense) from insertions and deletions (which cause frameshifts)
I can explain that a frameshift usually changes every codon downstream, so it is often more damaging than a substitution
I can explain that mutations are the ultimate source of new alleles and variation, and can be neutral, harmful, or beneficial
